(1) the environment is a subjective construction and environmental assessment frameworks should enable the consideration of all environmental phenomena of interest to FRIS stakeholders and (2) the proposed framework provides a logical basis for the consideration of the environment in FRIS.

the identification of environmental phenomena that should be addressed in an FRIS initiative, rather than with the assessment of environmental consequences per se, and provides a logical basis to do so.

we propose a logical basis accommodating the polysemous, relative and subjective construction of the environment in the context of FRIS.
environmental assessment frameworks used within the FRIS process should be based on an explicit logical basis that allows the subjective identification of environmental consequences.

a generic environmental assessment framework should be used to identify environmental phenomena of interest and to select environmental indicators for an FRIS process.
environmental assessment frameworks should be designed to accommodate all FRIS stakeholders' subjective perception of the environment and its phenomena of interest.
